title: Fix new-photo save failure in Android v1.1.4
description:
## Report
On the released Android v1.1.4 (code 4, source 700be08920ba4c7e9dee3b05b5c40c3dafb147aa), the user reports that the Encrypt existing photos action succeeds, but taking a new photo fails with "Photo could not be saved". Migration success is a user-reported observation; the capture root cause is not established. Previous mocked camera/coordinator tests did not reproduce this physical-phone failure.

## Scope
Trace the real Expo SDK 52 camera capture -> JS save helper -> Expo PhotoVault bridge -> native capture coordinator/codec path. Build a tight reproducible failure or identify a concrete broken prerequisite before making the smallest correction. Use the released artifact and installed Expo sources as evidence, not an assumed camera-cache path. Preserve migration/view/share behavior and fail-closed encryption. If a device trace is genuinely required after local attempts, report the specific missing nonsecret evidence rather than inventing a root cause.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Reproduce the confirmed defect with synthetic data through the relevant production boundary, including actual SDK URI/path or release-packaging assumptions rather than only an injected coordinator layout.
- A new capture saves as authenticated ciphertext and reopens through the encrypted viewer; both first-use and an already migrated vault work.
- Preserve the only recoverable original on failure, existing encrypted photos and key identity. No plaintext-gallery fallback, automatic key reset, broad path-validation weakening or private paths/image bytes/keys in logs.
- Add a focused regression that fails before the fix and passes after; run applicable existing JS/typecheck/lint and native build/runtime gates. Distinguish compile, mocked boundary, Android runtime and physical-phone proof.

## Authorization
User explicitly requested this ticket and an agent to investigate/fix it now. One bounded worker owns ONLY this save bug. Parent owns review, commits, publication and closure. No version bump/signed release, AGENTS edits, personal-photo access, migration-button UI work, dependency cleanup or other backlog changes.

title: Protect encrypted-vault backup and key-loss behavior
description:
## Scope
Make backup/restore, key invalidation and private-cache lifecycle honest and safe once the storage/share seams exist. Define Android backup exclusions for device-bound key material/ciphertext and temporary plaintext exports, including appropriate regenerated native configuration. Prefer explicit nonrecoverability over a misleading backup that restores undecipherable files. Explain uninstall, device changes and biometric changes according to the chosen actual key policy; do not claim recovery without a real key recovery mechanism.

Acceptance: backup config is visible in the generated Android manifest/rules and excludes sensitive temporary exports; missing/invalidated keys never trigger destructive reset/automatic replacement for an existing vault. Viewer/migration errors preserve recoverable files. README/PRIVACY/About accurately describe encryption, sharing and data-loss limitations after the feature is actually wired. Include focused config/key-loss handling checks within this implementation. Do not add cloud backup/recovery, new passwords, relock behavior or a general lifecycle framework.

title: Publish personal F-Droid repository and documentation together through CI
description:
## Approved Distribution Decision
Use a developer-operated F-Droid binary repository alongside the existing GitHub Pages docs, not the default f-droid.org catalogue. The user requires no manual steps between deployments. Normal Google Play API submissions can be automated, but Google explicitly documents states after rejected updates that require sending changes for review through the Console; do not promise zero intervention or add a Play-only route. One-time signing/repository setup is allowed as a prerequisite, not recurring release work.

## Scope
Extend .github/workflows/pages.yml and add minimal distribution/fdroid metadata/config and scripts. Target https://secret-camera.standen.link/fdroid/repo/ while retaining the README landing page and PRIVACY.html. Consume verified stable APKs from the tag-release workflow and generate signed F-Droid indexes with pinned fdroidserver tooling.

## Acceptance Criteria
- After setup, a valid release tag automatically builds/signs/publishes the APK and updates the signed repo plus docs: no manual index regeneration, APK copy, web-console action or required environment approval.
- Keep the F-Droid repository signing key distinct from the APK signer, stable across deployments and private in CI secrets. Both fresh keys are now generated and configured; verify the index against FDROID_REPO_FINGERPRINT and APK against ANDROID_SIGNER_SHA256. Owner-only local recovery copies exist; arrange an independently recoverable backup before calling key recovery fully protected. Never publish key/config secrets or generate replacement keys on each run.
- One serialized Pages publisher assembles both docs and repository on every deployment. A docs-only main push must preserve/rebuild the repo, and an app release must preserve docs; no conflicting deployers or docs-only overwrite.
- Index metadata selects the latest stable CurrentVersion/CurrentVersionCode correctly, retains the latest three stable APKs initially, includes source/license/app description and verifies APK checksum/signing identity before indexing. No fake source-build recipe is required for this binary repo.
- Provide repo enrollment URL/QR and public fingerprint. Users enroll once; update notification/installation behavior depends on F-Droid/Android client capabilities and must not be called guaranteed silent installation.
- In implementation, verify live docs/index/APK URLs, index trust and a normal install/upgrade with synthetic photos as part of development acceptance. No standalone proof task.
- Document that this is a developer repo, not official catalogue inclusion; recheck current Android developer-verification/install requirements without pretending self-hosting removes every platform constraint.

## Sources
https://f-droid.org/docs/Setup_an_F-Droid_App_Repo/
https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9859654
https://developers.google.com/android-publisher/api-ref/rest/v3/edits/commit

## Authorization
Implementation authorized for this publishing chain by the user. Work in dependency order: sc-21g -> sc-5rc -> sc-k8v. Keep unrelated security/barcode tickets untouched. The orchestrator owns tracker edits, review and publication; do not invent historical version/signing evidence or expose credentials.
acceptance_criteria: Every release publishes a trusted F-Droid index/APK and docs in one noninteractive CI flow; docs-only pushes cannot erase the repo.

title: Build, sign and publish Android APK releases automatically from tags
description:
## Scope
Add .github/workflows/ci.yml and .github/workflows/release.yml plus minimal build/signing helpers. Pull requests receive secret-free checks/builds; protected stable v* tags run checks, generate Android with Expo prebuild, build with a pinned compatible Gradle/Android toolchain, sign and publish an immutable APK/checksums/version metadata to GitHub Releases. No iOS jobs, custom app updater or EAS cloud dependency is required.

## Acceptance Criteria
- After one-time approved signing/CI credential setup, a valid protected release tag is sufficient: no recurring workflow approval, console click, manual build/upload or version-counter step between deployments.
- User authorized a NEW app-signing identity and does not require upgrades from old installs. Use the freshly generated Android signing key configured in GitHub secrets and verify final APKs against ANDROID_SIGNER_SHA256. Fresh-lineage initial baseline is 0; preserve this new signer for all subsequent releases. Do not require the old PC keystore or EAS/Play history. title: Make Android release versioning deterministic and checked in
description:
## Context
app.json currently reports 1.1.1/versionCode 1, package.json reports 1.0.0, and eas.json uses remote version sourcing with production autoIncrement. The checked-in code therefore does not establish the highest versionCode ever distributed.

## Scope
Make app.json the single checked-in version authority, synchronize package.json/package-lock.json version metadata, and remove the competing EAS remote auto-increment path (use local sourcing if EAS remains). Add a small release/tag validator and concise contributor instructions; no custom release framework.

## Acceptance Criteria
- User explicitly authorized a fresh signing lineage and waived compatibility with old installs. The initial previous-version baseline is explicitly 0 for this NEW lineage, not a claim about old EAS/Play history. The first release may use committed versionCode 1; later releases must exceed the highest code already published under this new signer, derived automatically from verified release history.
- A stable vX.Y.Z tag must match the checked-in application version and a positive integer Android versionCode above the previous distributed version. Reject mismatches, duplicate/reused codes and prereleases accidentally targeting stable.
- Building the same tagged commit reads the same versionName/versionCode without an EAS counter or editing generated native files. Reproducible version metadata is required; byte-identical APK reproducibility is not implied.
- Preserve link.standen.secretcamera and provide actionable validation failures before publishing. Tests for one valid tag and representative invalid metadata belong in this task.

## Authorization

title: Encrypt private photos at rest and automatically decrypt for viewing and sharing
description:
## Scope
This is the grouping epic for the original encrypted-photo feature, decomposed into seven bounded implementation children. Do not assign the whole epic to one worker.

## Scope
Replace the plaintext copy behavior in app/utils/security.ts with authenticated encryption using maintained platform/library primitives and an Android Keystore-backed key strategy. Include app/components/CameraView.tsx, GalleryView.tsx and ImageView.tsx, storage helpers, cache/backup rules and user-facing security wording as needed. Preserve the current private photo directory or migrate it safely.

## Acceptance Criteria
- New stored photos (including persistent thumbnails, if any) are encrypted at rest; plaintext capture/decode intermediates are kept minimal, private and cleaned up. No custom cryptography or hardcoded/exported secrets.
- Existing plaintext photos migrate crash-safely and idempotently: verify durable readable ciphertext before deleting originals; failed/interrupted migration must not lose photos.
- After normal successful app authentication, gallery thumbnails and full-size viewing work automatically without a manual decrypt action.
- Share automatically decrypts only the selected photo to a temporary app-private export and sends a conventional JPEG/image through the existing Android share sheet with narrowly scoped URI read access. The recipient needs neither Secret Camera nor a password/decryption tool.
- Handle success, cancellation, failure, backgrounding and restart with a bounded cleanup policy; do not delete a shared temporary file before the receiver has had time to consume it. Never put plaintext exports into the public media library automatically.
- Document key loss/biometric-change/uninstall/backup behavior and fail visibly rather than silently replacing a lost key or claiming recovery is possible. No private image bytes, keys or decrypted paths in logs.
- Include focused synthetic-photo encrypt/reopen/view/share and migration checks in this implementation; no standalone proof ticket.


## Success Criteria
All seven child implementations are complete with their own checks: key lifecycle, authenticated file codec, transparent gallery viewing, encrypted capture, safe migration, automatic normal-image sharing, and backup/key-loss handling. The app must not be described as encrypted merely because its key adapter exists. Preserve the original feature requirements above.

## Authorization
Key lifecycle sc-5ht.1, codec sc-5ht.2, and encrypted gallery sc-5ht.3 are completed with their scoped checks. Encrypted capture sc-5ht.4 is now completed with scoped Android runtime proof. Encrypted sharing sc-5ht.6 is now completed with scoped Android runtime proof. Legacy-photo migration sc-5ht.5 is completed with scoped Android runtime proof. User now explicitly authorized ONLY final encryption child sc-5ht.7 backup/key-loss safeguards and accurate documentation. Photo import, unrelated cleanup and signed release remain separate and unauthorized by this kickoff. No automatic progression across children.
acceptance_criteria: All seven children satisfy the original encrypted-at-rest, safe-migration and transparent normal-image sharing requirements; no photo loss or misleading encryption claim.
close_reason: All seven bounded encryption children are closed with scoped source/build and Android runtime verification. Final safeguards implementation 90fd36c; API 35 suite 33 tests with zero failures/errors/skips, JavaScript suite 75 tests, Android CI and Pages passed. New capture, encrypted viewing, ordinary-JPEG sharing, explicit verified legacy migration and backup/key-loss safeguards are wired. Existing plaintext photos still require explicit migration. No personal photos migrated; no new signed phone release or human end-to-end phone UI journey claimed.

title: Relock private content when returning from background
description:

title: Show Encrypt existing photos only when eligible legacy photos remain
description:
## Request
Only show the Encrypt existing photos button when legacy photos actually need encrypting. The user reports the action worked, but it remains visible unnecessarily afterward.

## Scope
Use the canonical migration eligibility/count contract to show the gallery action only when at least one eligible direct legacy photo remains. Avoid a second divergent filename/eligibility implementation. Refresh eligibility when the gallery loads and after migration or gallery mutations; no automatic migration.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Hide for an empty gallery and an encrypted-only gallery, and while eligibility is unknown/loading rather than advertising a speculative action.
- Show when eligible legacy photos exist, including a mixed encrypted/legacy gallery; ignore metadata, directories, symlinks and unsupported entries according to native migration eligibility.
- Hide immediately after successful completion leaves zero eligible photos; retain/show it after a partial failure if eligible originals remain.
- Preserve authentication, single-flight/remount, navigation guards and recoverable files; add focused real Gallery UI regressions for legacy-present, no-legacy and post-migration refresh.

## Authorization

acceptance_criteria: Gallery migration action is visible if and only if confirmed eligible legacy photos remain, with correct post-migration/partial-failure refresh and focused UI verification.

title: Import selected Android photos into the private gallery
description:
## Scope
Import existing photos selected through the Android system photo picker into the private Secret Camera gallery. Support one or multiple selected images. Reuse the canonical private-photo storage/encryption path rather than creating a separate plaintext import store. This is ordinary image import, not encrypted-backup restore or cloud sync.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Import is available only after normal app authentication; selected supported images appear in the private gallery and full-image viewer.
- Copy selected images; never move, delete or alter originals. Explain that the originals remain in their existing gallery/storage and are not made private merely by importing.
- Imported photos use the same authenticated encrypted-at-rest storage path as new captures, with bounded private temporary files and cleanup; do not silently fall back to plaintext on failure or replace a missing vault key.
- Picker cancellation changes nothing. Unsupported/corrupt inputs and partial failures report which items failed without losing successfully imported items, overwriting existing vault photos or exposing private image data in logs/public media storage.
- Use Android picker-scoped access rather than requesting broad storage access when unnecessary. Preserve image orientation and usable image quality; document supported image formats.

title: Remove unused barcode-scanning native dependencies from Android releases
description:
## Context
The existing lock resolves expo-camera 16.0.14, whose Android build unconditionally includes com.google.mlkit:barcode-scanning:17.2.0 and androidx.camera:camera-mlkit-vision. This app does not scan barcodes. Removing a JS prop or unused import does not remove native dependencies.

## Scope
Upgrade Expo/expo-camera to a supported compatible baseline that offers native scanner disabling. Configure barcodeScannerEnabled: false and, for SDKs using prebuilt Expo modules, force expo-camera to build from source using the SDK-supported package.json autolinking buildFromSource setting. Keep configuration regenerable through Expo prebuild; avoid hand-editing ignored generated Android files. Audit any document/code scanner dependencies introduced by the upgraded SDK as well.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Camera capture, front/back switching and private-photo storage continue to work on Android; existing photos are preserved through any FileSystem API migration.
- The resolved release runtime classpath and packaged release APK no longer include the unused barcode/ML Kit scanning implementations; inspect both rather than relying on a boolean or R8 assumptions.
- Inspect compileOnly/build-time scanner dependencies too. Upstream may retain compile-only references even with the runtime feature disabled; record these explicitly and do not claim a completely scanner-free build graph or official F-Droid compatibility while such dependencies remain. If full graph removal needs a maintained source patch or different camera module, document/implement the smallest justified change within this ticket.
- Lockfile and supported Node/Java/Android settings are updated coherently; typecheck/diagnostics and a real camera smoke check accompany implementation, not a new proof ticket.
